01: Late autumn dusk at a long roadside pavilion after a sudden rain has just stopped. A cicada rests on a wet willow twig while drops fall from the dark eaves onto glistening flagstones. A small traveler in a loose indigo robe stands under the pavilion, body small in the frame, face not filling the picture. Cobalt puddles, a tomato-red pillar, muted green willow leaves.
02: Outside an ancient city gate, a farewell canopy with wine cups left untouched on a low table. Beside the river an orchid-painted wooden boat waits, and a boatman lifts one hand urging departure. A traveler and a companion linger, reluctant to part, shown from the side at a distance so faces stay small.
03: Close view of clasped hands and teary eyes looking at each other, mouths closed, unable to speak. Loose Song-style sleeves in tomato red and cobalt blue, one tear on a cheek, generous empty space around them, no face filling the whole frame.
04: A tiny wooden boat drifting into a vast misty river at dusk, heavy evening clouds, a wide southern sky. Willow haze along the far bank. The traveler seen from behind, very small against the huge sky and smoke-colored water.
05: A cold clear autumn evening. Yellow fallen leaves, an empty roadside pavilion, one lonely wine cup, bare branches and a few muted-green chrysanthemums. A solitary traveler sits with sleeves wrapped tight, quiet and sorrowful.
06: Night inside a small boat cabin. The traveler has just woken, an overturned wine cup nearby, pale moonlight through a round window. He looks around, unsure where the boat has stopped.
07: Dawn along a willow-lined riverbank. Morning wind bends long willow branches. A thin crescent moon still hangs in the pale sky. The wooden boat rests quietly against the bank.
08: A fine day long after the parting: flowering branches, clear warm light, a beautiful riverside path. The traveler walks alone, the place beside him empty, the lovely view feeling hollow.
09: The traveler stands alone at night beneath the moon, one hand half raised as if about to speak, with nobody beside him to listen. Quiet sorrow.
